checklist: Verify your contractor license is current and valid in SC
Confirm your liability insurance is active (certificate is conditional only when the listed condition applies at permit office)
Have the property address and legal parcel number ready
Know the project value/cost — required on most permit applications
Panel schedule showing existing and proposed circuits
Wire gauge and breaker size for each new circuit
Electrical diagram or one-line drawing (required for panel upgrades)
Utility disconnect location marked on plans

Confirm the required license is active and matches the application: Commercial contractor pulls the permit on the owner's behalf — the contractor's license and business information must appear on the application. No electrical contractor permit is needed for this scope because the job description says no electrical work.
Bring 2 copies of all documents to City of Charleston Inspections & Legal Department

common_mistakes: Starting exterior work before BAR/historic district approval is issued — Charleston can hold or reject the permit if the facade change was not reviewed first
Submitting the sign and awning as a generic building permit only — the sign usually needs its own permit/review path
Leaving out wind-load and attachment details for the awning — coastal Charleston reviewers will kick back incomplete structural submittals

Assuming Permit required for the resolved scope; confirm exact filing details with City of Charleston Inspections & Legal Department before starting work. because there is no electrical work — exterior signs and awnings still trigger permit review

Submitting permit application without verifying current contractor registration status — an expired or lapsed city registration will block your application silently. Verify your registration is current BEFORE submitting.

pro_tips: For Charleston historic district jobs, get BAR approval first or in parallel with permit prep so you do not lose a week waiting on a resubmittal.
Bring a clean facade elevation with the sign dimensions called out in inches — that is usually what gets reviewed fastest.
Have the awning manufacturer's wind-load and anchorage data ready; coastal reviewers care about attachment details more than the brochure photo.
Check your Charleston contractor registration renewal date before starting any permit application — registration lapses are the #1 avoidable rejection reason.
